compare.topic: Council push to limit when SAPD contacts ICE

headlines.headline: Three council members try to limit SAPD contact with ICE
headlines.summary: Same proposal, four angles. News 4 leads with conflict and a public safety warning, the Report with momentum after Democratic wins, KSAT with the withdrawal, TPR with local pushback. Why compare: the verb a writer picks, split, follow, withdraw or push back, decides who looks in control.

breaking.headline: Woman shot and killed at a South Side apartment; police search for a 40 year old man
breaking.summary: A woman in her 30s was shot and killed just before 10:30 a.m. Wednesday in the doorway of an apartment in the 6200 block of South New Braunfels Avenue, near Pecan Valley Drive. Police say the shooter is a 40 year old man who fled in an older, dark colored Chevrolet Suburban, and he had not been arrested as of late morning. Three children were inside and are in Child Protective Services' care. Neither the woman nor the man police are seeking has been identified.

breaking.headline: Thanksgiving travel rush hits San Antonio's airport, with about 130,000 flying this week
breaking.summary: San Antonio International expects about 130,380 passengers from Sunday, Nov 22, through Sunday, Nov 29, with Wednesday, Nov 25, and Sunday, Nov 29, the busiest days. FOX 29 reported Wednesday morning that thousands of travelers were heading through the airport the day before Thanksgiving. Travelers should arrive two hours before domestic flights and three hours before international ones, and updates are at FlySanAntonio.com.

top.headline: Failed school tax votes mean 200,000 corrected tax bills
top.summary: Tax measures failed in Northside, San Antonio ISD, East Central and South San Antonio ISD, so October bills that assumed they would pass must be redone. About 200,000 Bexar County owners get corrected bills, posted online before Nov 30 and mailed around Dec 1. About 10,000 who already paid get refunds, averaging about $35 countywide. Bills are still due at the end of January.

top.summary: ICE detained a 54 year old man, named by ICE as Edgar Mortera Ambrosio Jr., at the city owned Culebra Bulky Waste Collection Center around 9 a.m. Thursday, Nov 19. Councilman Ric Galvan calls it likely the first ICE enforcement operation on city property, and Mayor Gina Ortiz Jones said in a KSAT interview that the arrest involved no city association. ICE says it did not choose the site and the man pulled in after agents stopped his vehicle, while Galvan says camera footage showed an unmarked vehicle stopping the family there. The footage has not been released, so where the stop began is not confirmed.

politics.summary: A council committee advanced a proposal for more public reporting on SAPD interactions with immigration authorities, with a full Council vote set for Dec 3. SAPD plans to begin expanded monthly reporting on Dec 1. Police figures show detainers for 54 of more than 42,000 arrests from January through October. The city is also suing over a planned 1,500 person detention facility on the East Side, with a status update due to a federal judge by Nov 30.

Mayor Gina Ortiz Jones is asking the Planning and Community Development Committee to consider a six month pilot with no exemptions. Veterans describe units in less desirable areas, loopholes, delayed payments and extra inspections.

politics.summary: District 1 Councilwoman Sukh Kaur filed a request for a no surprises construction policy after complaints about unexpected road work. Companies closing streets or sidewalks for more than a week would get a standard permit, share closures with navigation apps and send text alerts. Small businesses hit by closures over a month would get stakeholder meetings. Staff review comes first, then the governance committee in December or January.

Park leaders say the move could have major repercussions, while the city says housing discussions are very early. The park's leaders say Council approval is required. Ben Robertson will lead the civil division, replacing Larry Roberson. Chapa campaigned on overhauling the office's management, and retiring DA Joe Gonzales gave his final address to Commissioners Court on Tuesday, Nov 17. Commissioners Court has already moved one Gonzales lieutenant out of her authority.

artistry.summary: The San Antonio Stock Show and Rodeo named Parker McCollum and Lyle Lovett as its final two performers for 2027. McCollum plays Wednesday, Feb 17, at 7 p.m., and Lovett Saturday, Feb 27, at noon. The rodeo runs Feb 11 to 28 at the Frost Bank Center and Freeman Coliseum grounds, and Keith Urban headlines Feb 20.

artistry.headline: City seeks its next poet laureate and raises the stipend to $7,500
artistry.summary: San Antonio is taking nominations for its 2027 to 2030 poet laureate through 4 p.m. Dec 23. The annual honorarium rises to $7,500 from $3,500. The Department of Arts and Culture runs the search, and the new poet laureate is expected to be invested in April.

artistry.headline: Scaffolding will cover the Alamo's facade through the holidays
artistry.summary: Multi level scaffolding will stay on the Alamo Church facade through the holiday season while restoration continues under the half billion dollar Alamo Plan. Christmas in the Plaza still runs Saturday, Nov 28, from 6 to 8 p.m., with the tree in front of the scaffolded church. Scaffolding also went up at Mission Concepcion, where visitors use a side door until Dec 12.

artistry.headline: NIOSA organizers weigh a 2028 return at a new site
artistry.summary: The Conservation Society of San Antonio, which ran Night in Old San Antonio for more than 70 years, says it would like to bring NIOSA back in 2028. President Betty Bueche told the San Antonio Business Journal the group is still studying feasibility, including financing and organization, and no plans are final. The revival would likely not be held in La Villita, and no new site has been named. The society canceled the 2027 event in September and ended its La Villita agreement with the city in October.

artistry.summary: Centro San Antonio is expanding the one day shirt celebration to April 20 to 23, 2027, the same Fiesta dates NIOSA would have used. It will have three stages, vendors and food from 5 to 10 p.m. nightly. The move follows the Conservation Society's NIOSA pause and the city ending its La Villita lease. Part of the revenue will go toward preserving the historic village.

artistry.summary: The College of Education and Human Development now sits together in the Durango Building at the Downtown Campus for the first time. It enrolled nearly 1,700 students in fall 2025. revolution.headline: VIA rides are free Dec 1 in honor of Rosa Parks
revolution.summary: VIA will run fare free on all bus, VIAtrans and VIA Link trips on Tuesday, Dec 1, and every vehicle will keep its headlights on through the day for Rosa Parks Day. Parks was arrested on Dec 1, 1955, for refusing to give up her bus seat, which sparked the Montgomery bus boycott. VIA's board voted in 2019 to mark the day each December, and every VIA bus carries a front seat dedicated to her. VIAtrans riders must book trips ahead.

refs.t: VIA honors Rosa Parks with fare-free service on Dec. 1

revolution.summary: Leaders unveiled a three block district in Prospect Hill with a chapel, a Plaza of the Immigrants and the Mercado Corazon del Pueblo. Former Mayor Henry Cisneros said it affirms immigrant contributions. Private donors paid for it. The San Antonio Report reports the mercado opens Saturday, Nov 28, at 2203 W. Commerce St., the chapel is expected in February, and the plaza within a year or more.

revolution.headline: Sacred Heart Heritage District honors West Side immigrants

revolution.summary: Some immigrant families who attended immigration court in San Antonio are now being ordered to appear at the Dilley detention center, about 75 miles south of the city. Families not in custody must travel to a detention facility, and hearings run Monday through Friday inside it. One hearing was moved up from 2028 to November 2026 with six days notice. A San Antonio pastor says about 40 of her congregants have been detained in two years.

refs.t: Immigration court hearings move to Dilley detention center, raising concerns for San Antonio families

revolution.headline: Immigration court hearings move to Dilley, raising concerns for San Antonio families

revolution.summary: The San Antonio Housing Trust is removing the giant neon sign from the 10 story Robert E. Lee building at 111 W. Travis St., which is being renamed the Emerald on Travis. The city granted administrative approval for the name and sign change, but the trust still needs approval from the Historic and Design Review Commission. The trust bought the building in 2025, and all apartments will be reserved for households earning under 60% of area median income. No removal date has been announced.

community.summary: TxDOT will close the southbound I-35 inside and center lanes from George Beach Avenue to Frost Bank Center Drive nightly from 9 p.m. to 5 a.m., Sunday, Nov 29, through Monday, Dec 7. The northbound outside lane and entrance ramp also close nightly in that window. The northbound right turn lane to Frost Bank Center Drive closes around the clock from Nov 29 to Dec 18 for gas line work, part of the I-35 Northeast Expansion.

community.headline: San Antonio Zoo welcomes Mary Pat, an eight month old jaguar
community.summary: The San Antonio Zoo has a new eight month old female jaguar named Mary Pat, who came from Wildlife World Zoo, Aquarium and Safari Park in Arizona. Keepers are working one on one with her to build trust, and she could make her first public appearance as soon as Thanksgiving Day. community.summary: The San Antonio Food Bank says its holiday drive has reached about half of a 4 million pound goal, and the drive runs through Nov 30. Every $1 donated provides 10 pounds of food. business.summary: About 18,000 people have joined the city's Ready to Work program since it began almost four years ago, and about 6,500 have landed approved jobs, 43% of the program's goal. Leaders say average participant income rises from about $11,000 to about $45,000. The city's Status of Poverty report says 44% of Bexar County can't afford essentials. City Manager Erik Walsh said the city is still working through the state share with TxDOT, and the scaled back 2027 bond is too small to pay for the I-37 work alone. Spurs chief legal officer Bobby Perez said the team feels good about the project's direction. No date is set for a TxDOT decision.

The project grew from 42 planned sites to 52, with 35 finished. It should save about $1.8 million a year and offset roughly 11% of electricity use at city buildings.
